question: What is the primary goal of the home health care team?

options.A: To manage hospital facility budgets and supplies
options.B: To provide round-the-clock bedside nursing surveillance
options.C: To replace long-term hospital admission permanently
options.D: To maximize patient independence and restore health

explanation: Home health care focuses on promoting and restoring health while helping patients remain as independent as possible in their own homes. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why does home health care require high autonomy from its practitioners?

options.A: Patients refuse to follow direct orders from institutional doctors
options.B: Clinicians operate outside of constant, direct institutional supervision
options.C: Transportation challenges delay emergency physician responses always
options.D: Community health laws forbid supervision by senior medical staff

explanation: Home health staff visit patients independently and must rely on their own clinical judgment during visits without immediate backup. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h1)

question: Who is primarily responsible for establishing the initial nursing care plan in the home?
explanation: Registered nurses possess the advanced educational preparation required to conduct initial assessments and establish care plans. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h2)

question: A registered nurse notices a worsening pressure ulcer during a home visit. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Evaluate the wound, document findings, and notify the physician
options.B: Prescribe a stronger antibiotic ointment for immediate application
options.C: Discharge the patient from home care services immediately
options.D: Wait for the physical therapist to treat the skin breakdown

explanation: The registered nurse must assess changes in clinical status and report them to the primary provider to adjust the treatment plan. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h2)

question: What task is appropriate for a home health aide to perform?

options.A: Performing a comprehensive nursing admission assessment
options.B: Administering initial wound care for surgical incisions
options.C: Adjusting complex intravenous medication flow rates
options.D: Assisting the patient with daily bathing and grooming

explanation: Home health aides are trained to assist with personal care and activities of daily living rather than complex medical tasks. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why is the home health aide uniquely positioned to report early signs of clinical deterioration?

options.A: They conduct weekly laboratory blood draws for the agency
options.B: They prescribe medications when the registered nurse is absent
options.C: They hold advanced diagnostic credentials in internal medicine
options.D: They spend extended time observing the patient during personal care

explanation: Because aides assist with close-contact activities like bathing, they often notice subtle changes in physical condition first. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which professional specializes in helping patients recover fine motor skills for daily dressing?
explanation: Occupational therapists focus on fine motor tasks and activities of daily living like dressing and meal preparation. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h4)

question: A stroke patient struggles with coughing and choking while swallowing food. Which therapist should be consulted?
explanation: Speech-language pathologists evaluate and treat swallowing disorders, known as dysphagia, to prevent aspiration. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is a primary responsibility of the medical social worker in home health?

options.A: Administering intravenous antibiotic therapy for severe infections
options.B: Connecting patients with community resources and financial assistance
options.C: Conducting physical therapy gait training for fall prevention
options.D: Performing sterile dressing changes on surgical wounds

explanation: Medical social workers evaluate psychosocial needs and link patients to financial aid, food programs, and community support. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h5)

question: A patient cannot afford prescribed maintenance medications. Who is best suited to resolve this issue?
explanation: Social workers specialize in overcoming financial barriers and connecting patients with assistance programs for medications and supplies. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is interprofessional communication particularly challenging in home health care?

options.A: Electronic health records are strictly prohibited in community practice settings
options.B: Team members work independently in separate locations and visit at different times
options.C: Hospital administrators forbid community nurses from speaking with therapists
options.D: Physicians refuse to read notes written by non-nursing personnel

explanation: Since practitioners operate independently in the field, structured communication tools are vital to prevent gaps in care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of holding regular team conferences in home health care?

options.A: To assign daily administrative duties to office-based secretaries
options.B: To discipline staff members who fail to complete paperwork on time
options.C: To review patient progress and coordinate unified treatment goals
options.D: To reduce the total number of nursing visits required each month

explanation: Team conferences bring all disciplines together to evaluate outcomes and keep everyone aligned on the care plan. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h6)

question: Who acts as the primary daily caregiver between professional home visits?
explanation: Family members and the patient shoulder daily care responsibilities between scheduled visits from healthcare professionals. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the main benefit of actively involving family caregivers in the care planning process?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for professional nursing visits
options.B: It improves patient safety and reduces avoidable hospital readmissions
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing medical equipment
options.D: It transfers all legal liability for medical errors to the family

explanation: Educating and involving caregivers ensures proper daily management, which helps prevent complications and hospitalizations. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h7)
